2024_19_2_a_24680_troy_school_district_a.paragraph: Troy School District's Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, prepared by the Department of Business Services and given an unmodified opinion by Plante & Moran on October 28, 2024. Governmental activities recorded a $45,767,497 increase in net position, narrowing the district's net position deficit from $(162,472,077) to $(116,704,580), largely because its share of the MPSERS net pension liability fell to $288,852,665. General Fund balance rose $4,154,206 to $36,774,527, or 19.2 percent of 2024 general operating expenditures, while combined governmental fund balance fell $8,194,886 to $229,493,576 as the district spent proceeds of the $555 million bond approved in November 2022.
2024_19_2_a_24680_troy_school_district_a.page:
**Report, auditor, and officials**

Annual Comprehensive Financial Report of Troy School District for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, prepared by the Department of Business Services at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Transmittal letter dated October 28, 2024, signed by Dan Trudel, Assistant Superintendent Business Services, and Aurel Malutan, Director of Finance. Plante & Moran issued an unmodified opinion dated October 28, 2024; there were no findings or questioned costs for federal awards. ASBO International awarded a Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the FY2023 report (recognition held for fiscal years 1989-2023).

Board of Education: Karl Schmidt (President), Vital Anne (Vice President), Gary Hauff (Secretary), and Trustees Dr. Nicole Wilson, Emina Alic, Esq., Matt Haupt, Esq., and Dr. Nancy Philippart. Superintendent Richard Machesky, Ed.D.

**Government-wide results (governmental activities, in millions)**

| Item | 2024 | 2023 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total assets | 494.3 | 473.1 |
| Deferred outflows | 101.4 | 131.9 |
| Net pension liability | 288.9 | 340.4 |
| Net OPEB liability | - | 19.2 |
| Total liabilities | 621.0 | 700.4 |
| Deferred inflows | 91.4 | 67.1 |
| Total revenue | 267.9 | 224.6 |
| Total expenses | 222.1 | 208.8 |
| Change in net position | 45.8 | 15.8 |
| Total net position (deficit) | (116.7) | (162.5) |

Exact figures: total assets $494,266,679; total liabilities $620,909,433; net position deficit $(116,704,580) = net investment in capital assets $106,575,930 plus restricted $19,636,540 less unrestricted $(242,917,050). Expenses of $222,068,785 were offset by charges for services $5,914,344 and operating grants $79,485,003; general revenue was $182,436,935.

**Fund balances at June 30, 2024**

| Fund | Balance | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| General Fund | $36,774,527 | +$4,154,206 |
| 2023 Capital Projects Fund | $177,897,535 | -$10,783,131 |
| Nonmajor governmental funds | $14,821,514 | -$1,565,961 |
| Total governmental funds | $229,493,576 | -$8,194,886 |

General Fund revenue was $194,996,044 against expenditures of $191,469,703, plus $627,865 of other financing sources. Available fund balance equals 19.2 percent of 2024 general operating expenditures, above the board's 15 percent policy minimum. Two functions exceeded appropriations: support services-general administration ($2,635,590 actual vs. $2,424,946 budget) and community services ($163,173 vs. $147,065).

**Capital assets and debt**

Net capital assets $217,410,385 (gross $439,700,922 less $222,290,537 accumulated depreciation and amortization), up from $202,522,934; additions of $25.4 million and depreciation/amortization of $10,501,708. Construction in progress $21,750,478. Remaining contractor commitments $43,106,762 ($38,591,768 in the 2023 Capital Projects Fund; $4,514,994 in the Sinking Fund). General obligation bonds outstanding fell to $252,170,000 from $271,570,000; with $23,229,081 of unamortized premium, total bonds payable is $275,399,081. Remaining debt service to maturity is $401,657,563 ($252,170,000 principal plus $149,487,563 interest), final maturity May 1, 2052. S&P affirmed an AA/Stable rating in January 2024. Unqualified GO debt of $10.7 million sits against a $1.1 billion statutory limit; qualified debt totals $241 million.

**Retirement (MPSERS)**

Net pension liability $288,852,665 (proportion 0.89246 percent, measured September 30, 2023); net OPEB asset $(4,916,519) (proportion 0.86911 percent). FY2024 pension contributions $37,379,662, including $17,121,354 of state UAAL stabilization revenue; OPEB contributions $7,817,400. Pension expense $36,852,268; OPEB recovery $8,328,040. Discount rate 6.00 percent.

**Taxes, enrollment, and outlook**

Tax year 2023 taxable value $6,194,962,650 at 27.8415 mills; levy $76,169,213, 99.74 percent ultimately collected. Homestead operating 2.7764 mills, non-homestead 18.0000, debt 6.1000, sinking fund 0.9651. Tax abatements reduced revenue by $922,000, about $662,000 of it reimbursed by the state. Sinking fund collections were $4.9 million. Enrollment was 12,447 (Spring 2024); cost per pupil $15,383, revenue per pupil $15,666, average teacher salary $78,145. The 2024-2025 budget assumes 12,297 students and was built on a $241 per pupil foundation allowance increase, but the enacted state budget instead offsets MPSERS UAAL costs, worth $498 per pupil to Troy.
2024_19_2_a_24680_troy_school_district_a.verbose:
Troy School District's Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024 was presented to the Board of Education as agenda item 2.a. at the November 12, 2024 meeting. The report was prepared by the district's Department of Business Services at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (phone 248-823-4000, fax 248-823-4013); the transmittal letter, dated October 28, 2024, is signed by Dan Trudel, Assistant Superintendent Business Services (dtrudel@troy.k12.mi.us), and Aurel Malutan, Director of Finance. Plante & Moran, appointed by the Troy Board of Education for the 2023-24 fiscal year, issued an unmodified opinion dated October 28, 2024, concluding the statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the governmental activities, each major fund, and the aggregate remaining fund information. There were no findings or questioned costs for federal awards for the year ended June 30, 2024. ASBO International awarded Troy a Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the June 30, 2023 report, signed by President Ryan S. Stechschulte and CEO/Executive Director James M. Rowan, CAE, SFO; the district has held the certificate for fiscal years 1989 through 2023.

Officials. Board of Education: Karl Schmidt, President; Vital Anne, Vice President; Gary Hauff, Secretary; and Trustees Dr. Nicole Wilson, Emina Alic, Esq., Matt Haupt, Esq., and Dr. Nancy Philippart. Administration: Richard Machesky, Ed.D., Superintendent; Dan Trudel, Assistant Superintendent Business Services; Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent Secondary Instruction; Kristine Griffor, Assistant Superintendent Elementary Instruction; and John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent Employee Services.

Government-wide position. Total assets of $494,266,679 and deferred outflows of resources of $101,383,977 were offset by total liabilities of $620,909,433 and deferred inflows of $91,445,803, leaving a net position deficit of $(116,704,580) at June 30, 2024, an improvement of $45,767,497 over the prior-year deficit of $(162,472,077). Components were net investment in capital assets $106,575,930; restricted for capital projects $10,260,374, food service $3,600,167, debt service $859,480, and net OPEB asset $4,916,519; and unrestricted $(242,917,050). Assets included cash and cash equivalents of $53,840,373, due from other governments $27,685,252, restricted assets $189,182,996, and a net OPEB asset of $4,916,519. Deferred outflows comprised deferred pension costs $83,291,882, deferred OPEB costs $17,884,951, and deferred charges on bond refunding $207,144. Liabilities included accounts payable $12,134,183, due to other governmental units $4,670,705, accrued salaries and wages $11,086,288, accrued payroll taxes and fringe benefits $7,626,746, accrued interest payable $1,765,863, unearned revenue $6,928,277, noncurrent liabilities of $25,028,546 due within one year and $262,816,160 thereafter, and the net pension liability of $288,852,665. Deferred inflows were revenue in support of pension contributions made subsequent to the measurement date $17,121,354, deferred pension cost reductions $33,483,299, and deferred OPEB cost reductions $40,841,150. On the MD&A's rounded basis, total liabilities fell from $700.4 million to $621.0 million and the $19.2 million net OPEB liability of 2023 became an asset.

Statement of activities. Expenses totaled $222,068,785: instruction $121,913,991; support services $73,052,121; athletics $2,523,754; food services $6,085,533; community services $4,674,327; interest $13,816,434; and other debt costs $2,625. Charges for services were $5,914,344 and operating grants and contributions $79,485,003, leaving net program expense of $(136,669,438). General revenue of $182,436,935 included property taxes levied for general purposes $40,657,956, for debt service $30,460,375, and for capital projects $4,819,157; state aid not restricted to specific purposes $89,468,641; unrestricted federal grants $63,966; interest and investment earnings $12,502,005; gain on sale of capital assets $100,755; student activities $3,415,384; and other $948,696. Total revenue rose to $267.9 million from $224.6 million and expenses to $222.1 million from $208.8 million on the rounded basis.

Fund results. Combined governmental fund balance was $229,493,576, down $8,194,886 from $237,688,462. Governmental funds reported revenue of $260,195,511 (local $98,717,917; state $136,583,025; federal $12,574,899; interdistrict $12,319,670) and expenditures of $269,018,262, including instruction $127,256,676, support services $66,750,475, athletics $2,580,048, food services $6,032,043, community services $4,814,471, principal $19,505,606, interest $12,543,260, and capital outlay $29,533,058. The General Fund recorded revenue of $194,996,044, expenditures of $191,469,703, and other financing sources of $627,865 (leases entered into $527,110 and $100,755 from sale of capital assets), for a net change of $4,154,206 and an ending balance of $36,774,527 (unassigned $32,601,591; assigned for the subsequent year's budget $3,940,833). Available General Fund balance equals 19.2 percent of 2024 general operating expenditures against a board policy minimum of 15 percent. The 2023 Capital Projects Fund ended at $177,897,535 after $20,939,565 of capital outlay and $10,180,060 of local revenue. Special revenue fund balances rose from $9.7 million to $10.4 million: the Food Service Fund gained $0.6 million, primarily from federal supply chain assistance funds; the Community Service Fund lost $0.2 million; and the Preschool Fund added $0.4 million. Debt service fund balances rose $0.2 million combined, while capital project fund balances fell $13.3 million combined. Individual nonmajor balances were Food Service $3,600,167; Community Service $2,099,551; Troy Career Center $0; Preschool $2,291,052; Troy School and Student Activities $2,441,907; 2023 Debt $844,535; 2015 Refunding Debt $403,888; 2016 Debt $233,051; 2019 Debt $520,105; 2021 Refunding Series A Debt $1,167; 2021 Refunding Series B Debt $622,597; 2019 Capital Projects $1,014,912; Capital Maintenance $672,125; and Sinking Fund $76,457. Custodial (fiduciary) funds held $102,558 of cash with net position of $90,924 after additions of $186,787 and deductions of $188,725.

Budget. The final budget amendment was adopted in June 2024. Budgeted revenue was increased by $5.0 million, primarily state and federal, reflecting the 2024 State School Aid Act's full funding of Section 31a At-Risk revenue for hold harmless districts; expenditures were adjusted for 2023-2024 staffing levels and for retirement costs passed through the state under Section 147c. On the budgetary schedule, actual General Fund revenue of $195,623,909 exceeded the $193,048,749 final budget by $2,575,160, and actual expenditures of $191,469,703 came in $778,787 below the $192,248,490 final budget, producing an ending fund balance of $36,774,527 versus a budgeted $33,420,580. Two functions exceeded appropriations: support services-general administration, $2,635,590 actual against $2,424,946 budgeted, and community services, $163,173 against $147,065.

Capital assets and construction. Gross capital assets were $439,700,922 (land $1,861,010; construction in progress $21,750,478; buildings and improvements $358,803,377; furniture and equipment $56,228,659; lease asset-building $530,288; lease assets-equipment $527,110) less accumulated depreciation and amortization of $222,290,537, for net capital assets of $217,410,385, up from $202,522,934 in 2023. Additions totaled $25.4 million for building renovations, site work, furniture, equipment, and technology infrastructure. Depreciation and amortization of $10,501,708 was charged to instruction $4,600,562, support services $5,683,791, community services $106,536, food services $46,356, and athletics $64,463. Remaining contractor commitments totaled $43,106,762: $38,591,768 in the 2023 Capital Projects Fund and $4,514,994 in the Sinking Fund. The projects funded by the 2019 School Building and Site Bonds were considered complete on June 30, 2024, with cumulative construction-period expenditures of $26,703,725; the 2023 Capital Projects Fund is not yet substantially complete and a subsequent-year audit is expected. The district reported compliance with Section 1351a of the Revised School Code for the bonded capital projects funds and Section 1212 for the Sinking Fund.

Debt. General obligation bonds outstanding fell to $252,170,000 from $271,570,000 after $19,400,000 of reductions; with unamortized premium of $23,229,081, total bonds payable was $275,399,081. Outstanding series: the $31,930,000 2015 refunding qualified bond, $6,435,000 remaining at 5.00 percent maturing May 1, 2026; the $40,000,000 2016 qualified bond, $29,150,000 at 2.94-4.50 percent to May 1, 2032; the $7,125,000 2018 unqualified bond, $6,060,000 at 3.00-3.75 percent to May 1, 2040; the $22,630,000 2019 qualified bond, $17,425,000 at 5.00 percent to May 1, 2034; the $6,100,000 2020 unqualified bond, $4,645,000 at 2.00 percent to May 1, 2035; the $33,315,000 2021 refunding qualified bond, $24,505,000 at 0.50-1.56 percent to May 1, 2028; and the $171,370,000 2023 qualified bond, $163,950,000 at 2.75-5.00 percent to May 1, 2052. Remaining debt service to maturity is $401,657,563, comprising $252,170,000 of principal and $149,487,563 of interest, with $32,685,180 due in fiscal 2025. Standard & Poor's affirmed an AA/Stable rating in January 2024. The district's outstanding unqualified general obligation debt of $10.7 million is well below the $1.1 billion statutory limit (15 percent of assessed value); qualified debt totals $241 million. Other long-term liabilities were leases $690,681 (Troy Career Center building and equipment; $763,090 of future payments including $72,409 interest), compensated absences $7,896,313, other termination benefits $165,000, and a newly recorded arbitrage liability of $3,693,631 to be liquidated primarily by the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Total governmental long-term debt was $287,844,706 with $25,028,546 due within one year.

Deposits and investments. Restricted assets of $189,182,996 comprised unspent bond proceeds and related interest $184,841,180, unspent sinking fund property taxes $1,716,473, and unspent debt service property taxes $2,625,343. The district designated nine financial institutions and used three. Bank deposits of $40,535,431 were uninsured and uncollateralized. Investments carried at amortized cost were the Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Cash Management Money Market Fund $90,570,752 and MILAF MAX Class Money Market $102,724,121, totaling $193,294,873, both AAA-rated by S&P. Unearned revenue of $6,928,277 consisted of student lunch accounts $72,753, tuition and fees in advance $418,825, and grant and categorical aid received before eligibility requirements were met $6,436,699. The district participates in the SET-SEG shared-risk pool for property and general liability.

MPSERS pension and OPEB. The district reported a net pension liability of $288,852,665 (proportion 0.89246 percent, down from 0.90524 percent, a change of (1.41) percent) and a net OPEB asset of $(4,916,519) (proportion 0.86911 percent, down from 0.90842 percent, a change of (4.33) percent), both measured September 30, 2023 from a September 30, 2022 valuation rolled forward. Required and actual pension contributions for the year were $37,379,662, including $17,121,354 of state revenue remitted to fund the MPSERS unfunded actuarial accrued liability stabilization rate; OPEB contributions were $7,817,400. Pension expense was $36,852,268 and the district recognized an OPEB recovery of $8,328,040. Pension deferred outflows totaled $83,291,882 against deferred inflows of $33,483,299; OPEB deferred outflows were $17,884,951 against inflows of $40,841,150. Contribution rates ran 13.90-23.03 percent for pension and 7.06-8.31 percent for OPEB from October 1, 2023 through September 30, 2024. Key assumptions: entry age normal cost method, 6.00 percent investment return and discount rate, salary increases of 2.75-11.55 percent, health care cost trend of 6.25-7.50 percent grading down, PubT-2010 mortality with MP-2021 projection, and a 3.00 percent noncompounded COLA for MIP members. At a 5.00 percent discount rate the net pension liability would be $390,239,103; at 7.00 percent, $204,444,788. Year-end payables to the pension and OPEB plans were $7,976,870 and $1,201,887. Statutorily required contributions were $36,615,148 for pension (41.43 percent of $88,371,160 covered payroll) and $7,260,066 for OPEB (8.22 percent). Plan fiduciary net position reached 65.91 percent of total pension liability and 105.04 percent of total OPEB liability.

Taxes and statistical data. Tax year 2023 taxable value was $6,194,962,650 (residential $4,113,587,760; commercial $1,305,736,060; industrial $411,040,030; personal property $364,598,800) against $4,623,935,940 in tax year 2022, levied at 27.8415 mills with estimated actual value of $12,389,925,300. Direct millage in tax year 2023 was 2.7764 homestead operating, 18.0000 non-homestead, 6.1000 debt, and 0.9651 sinking fund, for 9.8415 total homestead and 25.0651 total non-homestead; overlapping rates included Oakland County 3.9686, community college 1.4891, intermediate school district 3.1658, State Education 6.0000, and City of Troy 9.8966. The FY2024 levy of $76,169,213 was 96.71 percent currently collected, rising to 99.74 percent ($75,972,515) with $2,311,543 of delinquent collections. Principal taxpayers were Somerset Collections ($63,920,120, 1.03 percent), DTE Electric Co. ($50,052,990), Lithia Real Estate Inc ($44,085,040), Troy Apts I-IV LLC ($33,682,460), Zen Troy LLC ($30,730,160), Midtown Place Troy LLC ($28,540,680), Pentrecentre LLC, MK Oakland Mall LLC, CC Troy Associates LLC, and Consumers Energy, together 5.75 percent of taxable value. Industrial facilities tax exemptions under PA 198 of 1974 and brownfield redevelopment agreements reduced property tax revenue by $922,000, of which approximately $662,000 was reimbursed by the State of Michigan. Net general bonded debt was $272,773,738, or 4.40 percent of taxable value and $3,098 per capita; direct and overlapping debt totaled $271,841,016, including City of Troy $10,014,855, Oakland County $9,709,634, and Oakland ISD $2,571,870. The legal debt margin was $918,539,398.

Operations and enrollment. Spring 2024 enrollment was 12,447 across twelve elementary schools, four middle schools, two traditional and one non-traditional high school, and International Academy East, occupying 448.74 acres and 2,185,181 square feet plus 128.30 acres of vacant property. Building enrollments include Troy High School 2,030 (343,207 square feet, built 1992), Athens High School 1,476 (398,426 square feet, 1974), International Academy East 539, Troy College and Career High School 160, Boulan Middle 832, Larson Middle 821, Smith Middle 644, Baker Middle 643, the Preschool/Early 5s building 222, and Troy Center for Transitions 70. Operating expenditures per pupil were $15,383 and operating revenue per pupil $15,666; average teacher salary was $78,145; 17.51 percent of students qualified for free or reduced meals; teaching staff numbered 887 and total FTEs 1,078; the fleet totaled 74 buses. Troy's population was 88,051 with 3.50 percent unemployment; the largest employer was Corewell Health Beaumont Troy Hospital (3,260 employees, 5.43 percent), with Troy School District second at 1,338 out of total employment of 60,058.

Outlook. The 2024-2025 budget, adopted in June 2024, assumes a September 2024 count of 12,297 students, with roughly 66.6 percent of General Fund revenue from the foundation allowance and state sources. The budget was built assuming a $241 per pupil foundation allowance increase, but the enacted state budget provided no foundation allowance increase and instead offsets MPSERS UAAL expenditures, equivalent to $498 per pupil for Troy; the transmittal letter describes the resulting retirement-rate change as worth about $4.7 million and warns the funding is one-time in nature. Voters approved a $555 million bond on November 8, 2022, to be issued in three series over six years with projects planned over 10 to 12 years; the first series was issued in March 2023, and the district expects to exhaust remaining 2013 bond funds in the next fiscal year. Sinking fund millage collections were $4.9 million in 2024. Management notes continued labor-market pressure on custodial, food service, transportation, and special education support staffing, and anticipates difficult decisions to keep the budget balanced. GASB Statements 101 and 102 take effect for the year ending June 30, 2025 and Statement 103 for the year ending June 30, 2026.
